enr_notes.basis: ENR 20-city Construction Cost Index, 1913=100. Annual averages unless a month is given.
enr_notes.1967-1999: ENR 'Construction Cost Index History (1908-2005)' as hosted by US EPA: https://semspub.epa.gov/work/07/40221155.pdf (p.1 monthly 1990-2005, p.2 annual 1908-1989).
enr_notes.1978-10: Converted: Gumerman report gives CCI 265.38 (1967=100) for Oct 1978 (report p.8); x 1074/100.
enr_notes.2023-09: TWDB UCM User Guide 2024, cost summary example, pdf p.40: 'ENR CCI 13485.67 for September 2023'.
enr_notes.2025-09: UNVERIFIED: value seen only in a search-engine snippet of ENR's Sept 22 2025 Construction Economics PDF (enr.com blocked, 403). It is consistent with ENR-reported annual changes (+0.9% 2024, +3.6% 2025 Dec-to-Dec). Confirm before use. 2021 and 2024 annual averages could not be fetched from a public source.

aace.source: AACE RP 18R-97 (paywalled) as summarized in City of Phoenix W/WW Unit Cost Study (Carollo, Aug 2024), Table 3, pdf p.14
aace.note: Ranges are typical; per AACE, accuracy range does not by itself define class. Curves here support Class 5 (and Class 4 when equipment counts/sizes come from the simulator).

items.source: TWDB Uniform Costing Model User Guide v3.0 (March 2024), Appendix: 'TWDB UCM Update: Proposed Unit Cost Updates' memo (Feb 27 2024)
items.notes: Power fit (R2=0.99, max err 5%) to booster column of Table 2. Includes contractor mobilization, OH&P; excludes engineering, contingency, land, ROW, permits. Above 50 mgd table is linear: cost = 8.763e6 + 57,950*mgd (50-700 mgd). Tables printed in Jan-2023 $; UCM indexes them to Sep-2023 CCI 13485.67 (Jan-2023 CCI not stated in the document), so enr_base slightly overstates the base (~1-2%).

items.source: TWDB Uniform Costing Model User Guide v3.0 (March 2024), Appendix: 'TWDB UCM Update: Proposed Unit Cost Updates' memo (Feb 27 2024)
items.notes: Linear fit (max err 0.5%) to booster column of Table 1. Intake (raw water) station column is ~3-6x higher at low hp. Same inclusions/exclusions and ENR caveat as C-PS-01.

items.item: Water booster pump station, single phase, construction cost
items.source: City of Phoenix Water and Wastewater Unit Cost Study, Final, Carollo, Aug 2024
items.notes: Fit (R2=0.98, max err 9%) to 'Construction Cost' column (direct cost + contractor OH&P, tax, general conditions; includes surge vessel and site work; excludes engineering, admin, permits, city fees). CMAR = x1.15. Costs updated to Sep 2023 with Handy-Whitman Plateau index; ENR value given for convenience.

items.item: Sewer lift station (submersible/wet well), construction cost
items.source: City of Phoenix Water and Wastewater Unit Cost Study, Final, Carollo, Aug 2024
items.notes: Fit R2=0.94, max err 24% (40 mgd point jumps). Use points for interpolation where possible.

items.source: US EPA WBS drinking water cost models (Adsorptive Media model WBS_adsorb_031323.xlsm, sheets 'Cost Coefficients' and 'Cost Data'; output labelled 'year 2021 dollars')
items.page: sheet 'Cost Coefficients' row pump_eq; data 'Cost Data' bls1141 Centrifugal Pumps (Booster)
items.notes: EPA's own fitted polynomial (R2=0.958). Vendor-quote averages; WBS escalates components with BLS PPI, not ENR, so enr_base left null (ENR 2021 annual average not verified). Not cost vs hp: convert with hp = gpm*TDH_ft/(3960*eff). No public cost-vs-hp curve for pump+motor found that met the quality bar; C-PS-02 gives whole-station cost per hp.

items.item: Variable frequency drive, installed retrofit on existing pump
items.source: Jones & Barrer, 'Efficiency Parameters for Variable Frequency Drives on Pumps in Open Systems', ACEEE Summer Study on Energy Efficiency in Industry, 1999, Table 2
items.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: only 3 points ($8,200 / $12,800 / $18,400 for 10/50/100 hp), total installed incl. integration with controls, stand-alone project. Old base year; escalate x ~2.3 to 2025. Better public VFD curve not found (utility rebate sheets give rebates, not costs).

items.notes: Linear fit exact to 0.3%. ~$11.9 per inch-diameter per LF + $67/LF. Above 30 in slope breaks (36 in $580, 48 in $893, 72 in $1,329/ft). UCM escalates pipelines with BLS PPI, not ENR. Excludes ROW, engineering, contingency.

items.item: Ductile iron water main, open cut, hard digging, with pavement replacement (urban Phoenix)
items.source: City of Phoenix Water and Wastewater Unit Cost Study, Final, Carollo, Aug 2024
items.notes: Power fit R2=0.97, max err 20%; use points. Includes trench, Class B backfill, pavement, fittings, valves, bypass, traffic control. Without pavement (Table 7): 6 in $210, 12 in $350, 24 in $780, 36 in $1,710/ft.

items.item: Ductile iron sewer force main, DUAL pipes, open cut, with pavement (Phoenix)
items.source: City of Phoenix Water and Wastewater Unit Cost Study, Final, Carollo, Aug 2024
items.notes: Cost per foot of corridor for TWO parallel force mains; halve only roughly for a single main (trench/pavement not halved). Poor fit (max err 25%); prefer points. HDPE: 4 in $790, 12 in $1,070, 24 in $2,260/ft.

items.item: Carbon steel pressure vessel (proxy for hydropneumatic / surge tank), equipment only
items.source: US EPA WBS drinking water cost models (Adsorptive Media model WBS_adsorb_031323.xlsm, sheets 'Cost Coefficients' and 'Cost Data'; output labelled 'year 2021 dollars')
items.page: sheet 'Cost Coefficients' row cs_pv_eq; 'Cost Data' bls1072 Carbon Steel Pressure Vessels - Stainless Steel Internals
items.notes: EPA fitted equation (R2=0.98). Vessels are treatment-media pressure vessels (ASME), used here as proxy for hydropneumatic/surge tanks; excludes installation, foundation, air compressor, controls. Plastic-internals variant: 17,250 (<=180 gal) to 142,935 (27,100 gal).

items.item: Gravity filtration structure (rapid sand/dual media), construction cost
items.source: Gumerman, Culp & Hansen, Estimating Water Treatment Costs Vol. 2, EPA-600/2-79-162b (Aug 1979)
items.notes: Fit R2=0.995. Table rows verified to sum to subtotal; total = subtotal x1.15 contingency. Excludes general contractor OH&P, engineering, land, special sitework. Points 140 sf=1 mgd ... 28,000 sf=200 mgd (at 5 gpm/sf). enr_base converted from report's ENR CCI 265.38 (1967=100, Oct 1978, report p.8) x 1074/100. OLD BASE: x~4.9 escalation to 2025 is a large source of error.

items.notes: Fit R2=0.985. G=20 (Table 39) slightly cheaper, G=80 (Table 41) dearer. Vertical turbine (Table 42) similar. Same old-base caveat as C-FIL-01.

items.source: Gumerman, Culp & Hansen, Estimating Water Treatment Costs Vol. 2, EPA-600/2-79-162b (Aug 1979)
items.notes: Fit R2=0.989; diameters 30-200 ft. Per basin. Rectangular clarifier (Table 46, p.134): cost = 1021.6*A^0.6477 for 240-4,800 sf per basin.
